nodes.characterization_summary: Cyclic voltammetry shows typical polycrystalline Pt surface features with distinct decrease in underpotential deposition hydrogen (H_upd) peaks and hydroxide adsorption/desorption peaks upon metal decoration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The cyclic voltammogram (CV) of the prepared Pt thin-film electrode in 0.1 M KOH (Figure 1b) shows the typical polycrystalline Pt surface features. The CVs of the PtM-low and PtM-high electrodes (Figures 1b and S4a-c) clearly show the distinct decrease of the area of underpotential deposition hydrogen (H_upd) peaks within the potential range from 0 to 0.45 V (from 0 to 0.2 V for PtMo electrodes) and the hydroxide adsorption/desorption peaks located at around 0.80 V compared to the undecorated Pt electrode.

nodes.characterization_summary: Hydrogen evolution reaction polarization curves measured in 0.1 M KOH show volcanic dependence of HER activity on surface oxophilicity, with Ru and Rh decoration promoting activity while Mo and Au decoration inhibit it.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figures 1c and S4d–f show the HER polarization curves measured in 0.1 M KOH, and Figure 1d gives the ratio of the current densities of PtM electrodes to that of Pt (denoted (j_PtM / j_Pt)_geo) at -0.035 V. It is apparent that depositing Ru adatoms onto the Pt surface exhibits a promotion effect on the alkaline HER activity, whereas the opposite is true for Mo and Au decorations.

nodes.characterization_summary: Density functional theory calculations of hydroxide adsorption free energies (ΔG_OH*) on various transition metal adatoms reveal the surface oxophilicity descriptor, showing volcanic relationship with HER activity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The hydroxide adsorption free energies (ΔG_OH*) on various transition metal adatoms were calculated via the DFT method (Figures 2a–e and S7–S8). Figure 2f illustrates that the experimentally measured (j_PtM / j_Pt)_geo at -0.035 V of PtM-low electrodes in alkaline conditions follows a volcanic dependence on the binding strength of hydroxide.

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic force microscopy images show that Pt thin-film electrodes decorated with various transition metals exhibit similar morphology characterized by islands of continuous Au nanoparticles approximately 50-100 nm in particle size with Pt or PtM nanoparticles densely wrapped around Au surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Exemplifying PtM-low, the atomic force microscopy (AFM) images show that the Pt thin-film electrodes decorated with various transition metals exhibit an overall similar morphology, which is characterized by islands of continuous Au nanoparticles, approximately 50 - 100 nm in particle size, with Pt or PtM nanoparticles densely wrapped around Au surfaces (Figure S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) measured from -0.05 to 0.20 V in 0.1 M KOH reveals interfacial water structures on decorated Pt electrodes, showing H-O-H bending vibration bands (δ_H-O-H) at ~1625 cm⁻¹ and O-H stretching vibration bands (ν_O-H) from 3000 to 3600 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3a-c shows the SEIRAS spectra of interfacial water molecules on the pristine and Ru-decorated Pt thin-film electrodes in 0.1 M KOH, which clearly display the H-O-H bending vibration bands (δ_H-O-H) located at ~1625 cm⁻¹ and the O-H stretching vibration bands (ν_O-H) from 3000 to 3600 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-SEIRAS analysis of O-H stretching wavenumber (ν_O-H) Stark tuning rate shows volcanic relationship with surface oxophilicity (ΔG_OH*), with Rh and Ru decoration increasing Stark tuning rate (weaker interfacial electric field) while Mo and Au decoration decrease it (stronger interfacial electric field).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figures 3e and S12, the ν_O-H peaks on various electrodes display a distinct red shift as the potential swept positively due to the inherent dipole moment of water and its Stark tuning effect. Interestingly, one can note that with increasing the deposition coverage, the Stark tuning rate of interfacial water molecules gradually increases on Rh- and Ru-decorated electrodes, while it decreases on Mo- and Au-decorated electrodes (Figure S13).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations of electrode/water interfaces show that surface oxophilicity triggers inverted volcano-type variation in potential of zero charge (PZC), with Rh and Ru decoration lowering PZC while Mo and Au decoration increasing PZC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4f shows that the PZC values on various electrodes exhibit an inverted volcano-type variation behavior with the surface oxophilicity, in which Au and Mo decoration indeed increases the PZC, while Rh and Ru decoration lowers the PZC compared to the pristine Pt electrode and Rh is at the apex of the volcano curve.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEIRAS spectra in CO-saturated 0.1 M HClO₄ show two C=O stretching peaks at ~2078 and 1875 cm⁻¹ assigned to CO on top and bridge sites of Pt surface, with no CO adsorption peak on Au substrate at ~2100 cm⁻¹, confirming Pt thin-film electrode quality and Au substrate non-interference.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEIRAS spectra measured in CO-saturated 0.1 M HClO₄ clearly exhibit two peaks at ~2078 and 1875 cm⁻¹ (Figure S2a), which are assigned to the C=O stretching modes of CO adsorbed on the top and bridge sites of the Pt surface, respectively, and no CO adsorption peak on Au that should be at ~2100 cm⁻¹ appears.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-SEIRAS spectra in CO-saturated 0.1 M HClO₄ after oxidation at 1.5 V versus RHE for 5 s show no reduction peak of oxide layer at ~1.15 V when potential scanned from 1.5 to 0.9 V, confirming Au substrate does not interfere with Pt thin-film electrode characterization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the electrodes were oxidized at 1.5 V versus RHE for 5 s, there was no reduction peak of the oxide layer at ~1.15 V on the prepared Pt thin-film electrode surface when the potential was scanned from 1.5 to 0.9 V compared to the Au film electrode.
